items.title: 1.2.1 Square Root of a Complex Number (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum ek complex number ka square root (jazr) nikalna seekhenge, aur ek aisa formula banayenge jo seedha jawab de de. Pichle sabaq (1.2) mein aap ne dekha tha ke do complex numbers barabar hon to un ke real parts aur imaginary parts alag alag barabar hote hain. Aaj ka poora formula usi rule par khara hai, is liye woh rule zehan mein taaza rakhiye.
Kitab ki definition: kisi complex number ka square root ek aur complex number hai jise square karein (khud se multiply karein) to asal complex number wapas mil jaye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh bilkul wahi idea hai jo aap real numbers mein jaante hain: 3, number 9 ka square root hai kyun ke \(3^{2} = 9\). Aur \(-3\) bhi, kyun ke \((-3)^{2} = 9\). Isi tarah \(w\) number \(z\) ka square root hai jab \(w^{2} = z\).
Har non-zero complex number ke bilkul do square roots hote hain: \(w\) aur \(-w\). Dono ek doosre ke negative hain.
Ab sawal yeh hai: \(5 + 12i\) jaise number ka square root andaze se kaise nikalein? Andaze se mushkil hai. Is liye neeche hum qadam ba qadam ek formula derive karenge (yani khud bana kar dekhenge ke kahan se aaya), taa ke aap use ratta na lagayein balke samajh kar use karein.
Deriving the formula

Sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke humein kya maloom hai aur kya dhoondna hai. Maan lijiye \(w = p + qi\) ek square root hai complex number \(z = x + iy\) ka, jahan \(p, q, x, y \in \mathbb{R}\) (sab real numbers). Yahan \(x\) aur \(y\) humein maloom hain (diya hua number), aur \(p\), \(q\) dhoondne hain. To \(w = \sqrt{z}\) ...(i). Dono sides ka square lene se:

Dekhiye yahan kya hua: \((p + iq)^{2} = p^{2} + 2p(iq) + (iq)^{2}\), aur \((iq)^{2} = i^{2}q^{2} = -q^{2}\). Yani \(i^{2} = -1\) ne \(q^{2}\) ko real part mein bhej diya. Ab dono sides (real) + (imaginary)\(i\) ki shakal mein hain, is liye equality ka rule laga sakte hain. Real aur imaginary parts barabar karne se:

\[x = p^{2} - q^{2} \quad \text{...(ii)}\]
\[y = 2pq \quad \text{...(iii)}\]

Ab humare paas do equations hain magar dono mein \(p\) aur \(q\) ulajhe hue hain. Inhein suljhane ke liye ek purani algebraic identity kaam aati hai. Hum jaante hain ke
\[(p^{2}+q^{2})^{2} = (p^{2}-q^{2})^{2} + 4p^{2}q^{2}\]
Is mein \(x = p^{2} - q^{2}\) aur \(y = 2pq\) rakhein (ghor karein: \(4p^{2}q^{2} = (2pq)^{2} = y^{2}\)), to
\[(p^{2}+q^{2})^{2} = x^{2} + y^{2}\]
\[\Rightarrow p^{2} + q^{2} = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}} \quad \text{...(iv)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh identity sahi kyun hai? Dono sides ko khol kar dekhiye: \((p^{2}+q^{2})^{2} = p^{4} + 2p^{2}q^{2} + q^{4}\), aur \((p^{2}-q^{2})^{2} + 4p^{2}q^{2} = p^{4} - 2p^{2}q^{2} + q^{4} + 4p^{2}q^{2}\), jo wahi \(p^{4} + 2p^{2}q^{2} + q^{4}\) ban jata hai. Dono barabar!
(iv) mein sirf positive square root kyun liya? Kyun ke \(p\) aur \(q\) real hain, aur real numbers ke squares kabhi negative nahin hote. Is liye \(p^{2} + q^{2}\) kabhi negative nahin ho sakta; minus wala root yahan bekaar hai.
Khud sochiye: \(\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) aap ne pehle kahan dekha tha? Haan, yeh \(|z|\) yani modulus (origin se faasla) hai. Yeh baat aage formula ko chhota karne mein kaam aayegi.

Ab equations (ii) aur (iv) ko saath rakhiye: \(x = p^{2} - q^{2}\) aur \(p^{2} + q^{2} = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\). Yeh simultaneous equations ki tarah hain jin mein \(p^{2}\) aur \(q^{2}\) unknown hain. Inhein jama karne se \(q^{2}\) khatam hota hai, aur ek doosre se tafreeq (subtract) karne se \(p^{2}\) khatam hota hai (yeh chhota step kitab chhor deti hai):
\[2p^{2} = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}} + x\]
\[2q^{2} = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}} - x\]
Ab dono ko 2 se divide kar ke square root lein, to \(p\) aur \(q\) ki values yeh hain:

blocks.text_alt: p equals plus or minus the square root of (square root of x squared plus y squared, plus x) over 2
q equals plus or minus the square root of (square root of x squared plus y squared, minus x) over 2

blocks.text: Lekin ab ek masla hai: \(p\) ke do signs aur \(q\) ke do signs, yani chaar combinations. Jab ke square roots sirf do hote hain! To sahi jori kaun si hai? Iska faisla equation (iii) karti hai: \(y = 2pq\). Is liye:

items: \(y > 0\) ho to \(p\) aur \(q\) ka sign same hoga (dono positive ya dono negative)
\(y < 0\) ho to \(p\) aur \(q\) ke sign ulte (opposite) honge

blocks.text: Wajah seedhi hai: do numbers ka product tabhi positive hota hai jab un ke signs same hon, aur negative tab jab signs ulte hon. In sab baaton ko jor kar complex number \(z = x + iy\) ka square root yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: square root of x plus i y equals plus or minus, open bracket, square root of (square root of x squared plus y squared, plus x) over 2, plus i y over modulus of y times square root of (square root of x squared plus y squared, minus x) over 2, close bracket

blocks.text: ya, \(|z| = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}} \ge 0\) (yani \(z\) ka modulus) likh kar, formula chhota aur yaad karne mein aasan ho jata hai:

blocks.text_alt: square root of z equals plus or minus, open bracket, square root of (modulus of z plus x) over 2, plus i y over modulus of y times square root of (modulus of z minus x) over 2, close bracket, equation (v)

blocks.text: Equation (v) hi complex number ka square root nikalne ka required formula hai. Ise yaad karne ka aasan tareeqa: "pehle modulus nikaalo; real part ke liye \(|z| + x\), imaginary part ke liye \(|z| - x\), dono ko 2 se divide kar ke root lo; aur sign \(y\) se tay karo."

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Formula mein \(\frac{iy}{|y|}\) dekh kar ghabraiye mat. Yeh sirf sign batane wala hissa hai: \(y > 0\) ho to yeh \(i\) hai, aur \(y < 0\) ho to \(-i\). Matlab:
agar \(y > 0\) to root ke real aur imaginary parts ka sign same;
agar \(y < 0\) to sign ulte.
Yeh formula \(y \ne 0\) ke liye hai (warna \(|y| = 0\) se divide karna parega). Agar \(y = 0\) ho to \(z = x\) real number hai: \(x > 0\) ke liye roots \(\pm\sqrt{x}\), aur \(x < 0\) ke liye roots \(\pm i\sqrt{-x}\). Misal: \(\sqrt{-9} = \pm 3i\).
Ab kitab ki misaal mein yeh formula chala kar dekhte hain, aur jawab ko Argand diagram par bhi dikhayenge.

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem: Find the square root of complex number \(5 + 12i\) and also represent the square roots on an Argand diagram.
steps:
Given: \(z = 5 + 12i\).
To find: \(z\) ke dono square roots, aur unhein Argand diagram par dikhana.
Method: sab se pehle yeh samajhte hain ke humein kya chahiye: aisa complex number jis ka square \(5 + 12i\) ho. Is ke liye formula (v) bilkul fit hai. Formula ko teen cheezein chahiye: \(x\), \(y\) aur \(|z|\). Aur \(y\) ka sign batayega ke root ke dono parts ke sign same hain ya ulte. Plan: pehle \(x, y\) pehchaanein, phir modulus, phir dono parts, phir \(\pm\) laga kar dono roots.

Step 1: \(x\) aur \(y\) pehchaanein
\[x + yi = 5 + 12i\]
\[x = 5,\quad y = 12 > 0\]
Kyun: formula (v) \(x\) aur \(y\) ki shakal mein likha hai, is liye pehle unhein alag karna zaroori hai. \(y = 12\) positive hai, is liye \(\frac{iy}{|y|} = \frac{12i}{12} = i\). Matlab root ke dono parts ka sign same hoga.

Step 2: Modulus nikaalein
\[|z| = |5 + 12i| = \sqrt{5^{2} + 12^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169}\]
\[|z| = 13\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) formula ke dono square roots ke andar aata hai, is liye ise pehle nikaal lena kaam aasan karta hai. Modulus ka formula \(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) hai (Pythagoras wala faasla).
Dhyan dein: \(|z|\) ek square root hai, \(169\) nahin balke \(13\). Bohat se students \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hi likh kar aage chal parte hain.

Step 3: Root ka real part
\[\sqrt{\dfrac{|z| + x}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{13+5}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{9} = 3\]
Kyun: yeh formula (v) ka pehla square root hai, jo derivation mein \(p\) tha. Real part ke liye hamesha \(|z| + x\) aata hai.

Step 4: Root ka imaginary part
\[\dfrac{12i}{|12|}\sqrt{\dfrac{13-5}{2}}\]
\[= i\sqrt{4} = 2i\]
Kyun: \(\frac{12}{|12|} = 1\), is liye sign wala factor sirf \(i\) hai. Phir \(\sqrt{(13-5)/2} = \sqrt{4} = 2\). Imaginary part ke liye hamesha \(|z| - x\) aata hai; minus aur plus ki jagah ulat dena aam ghalti hai.

Step 5: Square roots likhein
\[\sqrt{5+12i} = \pm\left(\sqrt{9} + i\sqrt{4}\right)\]
\[= \pm(3 + 2i)\]
Kyun: shuru wala \(\pm\) humein do square roots deta hai: \(3 + 2i\) aur \(-3 - 2i\). Ghor karein ke minus poori bracket par lagta hai, is liye doosra root \(-3 - 2i\) hai, \(-3 + 2i\) nahin. Dono ek doosre ke negative hain, bilkul jaise \(3\) aur \(-3\) dono \(9\) ke roots hain.

Step 6: Argand diagram par dikhayein
\(3 + 2i\) point \((3, 2)\) hai, pehle quadrant (pehla hissa, jahan dono coordinates positive hain) mein; \(-3 - 2i\) point \((-3, -2)\) hai, teesre quadrant mein (neeche figure dekhiye).
Kyun: Argand diagram par real part \(x\)-axis par aur imaginary part \(y\)-axis par naapa jata hai. Dono square roots hamesha origin \(O\) ke aar paar, bilkul aamne saamne hote hain: ek ko origin ke gird aadha chakkar (\(180^{\circ}\)) ghumayein to doosra mil jata hai.

Tasdeeq:
Ab dekhte hain ke jawab sach mein sahi hai ya nahin; square kar ke asal number wapas aana chahiye.
\[(3 + 2i)^{2} = 9 + 12i + 4i^{2}\]
\[= 9 + 12i - 4 = 5 + 12i\]
\[(-3 - 2i)^{2} = (3 + 2i)^{2} = 5 + 12i\]
Dono squares asal number dete hain, is liye jawab durust hai. (Doosre root mein \((-1)^{2} = 1\) ki wajah se minus khatam ho jata hai.)
blocks.answer: \(5 + 12i\) ke square roots \(3 + 2i\) aur \(-3 - 2i\) hain, yani \(\pm(3 + 2i)\); yeh points \((3, 2)\) aur \((-3, -2)\) par dikhaye gaye hain.

blocks.alt: Argand diagram with axes x′x and y′y marked from minus 4 to 4. The point 3 + 2i is plotted at (3, 2) in the first quadrant and the point minus 3 minus 2i at (minus 3, minus 2) in the third quadrant.
blocks.caption: Figure: the square roots 3 + 2i and −3 − 2i of 5 + 12i (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ab ek aisa number lete hain jis mein \(y\) negative hai, taa ke sign wala rule saaf ho jaye (yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin): \(z = 8 - 6i\).
\(x = 8\), \(y = -6 < 0\), is liye parts ke sign ulte honge.
\(|z| = \sqrt{64 + 36} = 10\).
Real part: \(\sqrt{(10 + 8)/2} = \sqrt{9} = 3\). Imaginary part: \(\sqrt{(10 - 8)/2} = \sqrt{1} = 1\), sign minus.
Jawab: \(\pm(3 - i)\). Tasdeeq: \((3 - i)^{2} = 9 - 6i + i^{2} = 8 - 6i\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(w\) number \(z\) ka square root hai agar \(w^{2} = z\); har non-zero number ke do roots hote hain: \(w\) aur \(-w\).
2. Formula (v): \(\sqrt{z} = \pm\left(\sqrt{\frac{|z|+x}{2}} + \frac{iy}{|y|}\sqrt{\frac{|z|-x}{2}}\right)\).
3. Real part mein \(|z| + x\), imaginary part mein \(|z| - x\).
4. \(y\) ka sign faisla karta hai: \(y > 0\) to parts ke sign same, \(y < 0\) to ulte.
5. Argand diagram par dono roots origin ke aar paar aamne saamne hote hain.
6. Jawab ko hamesha square kar ke check karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Sirf ek root likhna: roots hamesha do hote hain, is liye \(\pm\) zaroor lagayein.
2. \(y\) ka sign nazarandaz karna: \(8 - 6i\) ke roots \(\pm(3 - i)\) hain, \(\pm(3 + i)\) nahin. Bachne ka tareeqa: shuru mein hi likh lein "\(y\) positive hai / negative hai".
3. Formula ke andar \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) likh dena jab ke \(|z| = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) hai, yani square root.
4. \(-(3 + 2i)\) ko \(-3 + 2i\) likh dena: minus bracket ke dono terms par lagta hai.
